title: Customer on-prem network gateways prioritization & staged communications lane
creator: Samantha Green
description:
Summary: Create a prioritized lane and templated decision flow for customer requests that require on-prem/VPC networking changes (gateway/proxy installs, NAT traversal, edge connector proxies, scheduled kernel/firmware upgrades in air-gapped environments). Goal is to reduce manual triage time, surface clear acceptance criteria for fast-lane approvals, and provide deterministic comms playbooks for engineering and solutions teams.

Scope: non-bug customer requests that are about network readiness, scheduled on-prem upgrades, or air-gap constraints. Includes design of a risk/rank rubric, a staged communications ladder (customer -> SE -> security -> infra -> eng oncall), and automation to prepopulate readiness forms from a lightweight network probe. Excludes emergent security incidents and purely legal/POL review items.

Acceptance criteria: (1) A documented prioritization rubric that maps customer risk/profile to one of three lanes: Fast-track, Standard, and Remediation. (2) Templated email/slack communication snippets and a staging checklist per lane. (3) Lightweight network probe CR that the SEs can run (or customers can run) producing a compatibility score. (4) Pilot with 3 enterprise customers and measured reduction in triage time by >=40% for eligible requests.

Out-of-scope: Changes requiring full on-prem appliance installs or bespoke engineering work that exceeds a 40 hour scoping threshold.

Rationale: Our backlog shows high variance in time-to-response for network-dependent private deployments. Repeated friction is caused by inconsistent information from customer intake, unclear ownership for network troubleshooting, and lack of deterministic gating for upgrades. A staged lane reduces unblocker points while preserving security review.

Trade-offs: Tighter fast-lane criteria reduces the number of customers eligible but keeps operational load manageable. Automating the readiness probe lowers manual effort but may miss deep proxy/ACL quirks; we will surface raw probe artifacts to SEs for follow-up.

Decision records and links are in comments below.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff: Reviewed backlog and classified 28 recent requests. Agreed on three lane model and initial fast-lane criteria (customer-managed proxy + documented NAT mapping + support for TLS termination). Attendees: S. Green (PM), M. Rodriguez (SE lead), A. Patel (Security), L. Chen (Solutions).

2026-02-25 - Draft rubric posted to Confluence for feedback. Key ask from Security: require KMS/HSM note for any offsite key materials. Action: add a 'crypto custody' flag to the probe output. (Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Private/Network+Gateways+Prioritization)

2026-03-02 - Engineering sync: ENG requested explicit list of reachable ports and expected sequence lengths for KV cache warmups to validate kernel scheduling assumptions. Added 'service port matrix' to probe. (ENG tickets referenced in dependencies)

2026-03-04 - SE pilot recruited: Acme Financial (NDA), MediCore Health, and Atlas Logistics agreed to trial the staged-lane. SEs will run probe and file readiness report. Prepared templated comms in Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-network-templates
2026-03-08 - Legal/Compliance review: Suggested adjustments to data retention policy for probe artifacts. New requirement: probe artifacts retained for 90 days by default.
decision_log: 2026-02-27 - Adopted three-lane model: Fast-track (automated pass + legal pre-approval), Standard (SE-run probe + scheduled eng window), Remediation (requires engineering scoping).
2026-03-05 - Fast-track criteria finalized: (1) customer can expose endpoint via single NAT rule, (2) TLS termination within perimeter and certs validated, (3) no HSM dependency for initial rollout.
next_steps: Deliver network probe v0.1 and PR to the network-probes repo (owner: ENG-Infra, due 2026-03-22)
Update SE onboarding doc with templated comms and decision ladder (owner: Solutions, due 2026-03-15)
Run pilot with three customers and gather time-to-triage metrics (owner: M. Rodriguez, due 2026-04-05)
Formalize fast-lane SLA and publish to Console docs (owner: PM, due 2026-04-12)
notes: Pilot success metric: triage time <= 48 hours for fast-track and <= 5 business days for standard lane.
Fallback policy: if probe fails due to partial connectivity, system should auto-create a remediation ticket with prefilled environment artifacts and recommended next steps.
Consideration: integrate with onboarding dashboard to surface 'network readiness' score next to customer request in the console.
